mostWorthwhile.text: The grazing impact and subsequent moon formation were most worthwhile: the collision created orbiting debris, and gravity gathered some of it into a moon while other fragments fell back or escaped.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying the orbiting rubble on the molten world was least worthwhile as progress: it failed, although the compatibility feedback helped identify the next options.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the orbiting rubble could not form a moon immediately; another large impact first created a debris cloud around the world.

arbitrary.text: The need to develop a dense core before the moon-forming impact felt somewhat prescribed. Core formation was explained physically, but why it had to precede that impact was less clear.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue: the contrasting outcomes of impacts and the reassembly of shattered material made me curious about what happens to the remaining fragments.
